verdict.root_cause: Frontend PlaceOrder requests are failing because the cart dependency is refusing connections. Failing traces run 1.2-1.7ms and terminate at the checkoutservice -> CartService/GetCart span with ERROR on the whole ancestor chain and nothing recorded below it [tr_96ee5ce2de29], while frontend logs show gRPC code 14 UNAVAILABLE with 'no connection established' plus a detail line naming the checkout cart fetch and a refused TCP dial to a concrete address on port 7070 [tr_0271ca85f856]. Blame sits on cartservice: it resolves but is not accepting connections on a fraction of dials. Frontend and checkoutservice are reporting an unreachable dependency, not their own fault - checkoutservice's error ratio is flat-to-lower than baseline with no error logs at onset [tr_742a0e81c22a][tr_247ff21e0444], and frontend's errors are bursty with minima at zero [tr_fd630b3e661c]. Why cartservice refuses connections is not established: no cartservice logs, metrics, change history or process state were ever queried, so crash loop, limit kill, wrong bind address, or replica loss all remain open. I name the service and the mechanism (dependency unreachable by active connection refusal) but leave the class unknown.
verdict.reasoning: Two independent signals converge on one hop. Traces localise the abort at CartService/GetCart with checkoutservice self-time of ~0.1ms, which excludes checkout's own logic and every dependency ordered after the cart read - payment, email, currency, shipping and productcatalog are healthy or unreached [tr_96ee5ce2de29]. Frontend logs name the same dependency and give the mechanism: refused dial to IP:7070, not a timeout, DNS, or TLS/auth failure [tr_0271ca85f856]. Causality points away from the alerting services: frontend alerted first as the caller and its error ratio is the propagated symptom [tr_fd630b3e661c]; checkoutservice shows no error-rate departure and no error lines [tr_742a0e81c22a][tr_247ff21e0444]. Change history closes frontend as an actor [tr_167ae270c816], and the productcatalogservice shaping experiment was cleanly reverted 13.4h before onset [tr_809820cbb77d], consistent with failures being fast rejections rather than stalls. I stop short of a mechanism class because cartservice itself was never inspected; a restart of its replicas restores listeners under any of the candidate mechanisms, but may not be the durable fix.
open_questions: No cartservice evidence of any kind was collected, so the mechanism behind the refusal - crash loop, limit kill, wrong bind port, replica loss - is unsettled.

The same UNAVAILABLE pattern appears at ~20:56, before the 21:34 alert [tr_0271ca85f856], and all change queries began at or after 21:34 [tr_51c4169ff3a9], so true onset and any triggering act pre-onset were never searched.
Why only part of traffic fails (peak ~33%, minimum 0%) - partial replica loss versus intermittent restarts - is not distinguished by any result.

alternatives.root_cause: cartservice processes were killed for exceeding a memory or connection limit, and the restart gaps produce refused dials.
alternatives.why_not: No cartservice memory, connection or restart data was collected; refusal alone does not distinguish exhaustion from other listener-loss causes.

alternatives.root_cause: cartservice is running a broken or wrong artifact that fails to bind its listener, so dials are refused.
alternatives.why_not: No cartservice change history was queried, so no deploy exists in evidence to correlate; and partial success suggests some replicas do serve, which a uniformly unstartable artifact would not.

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no effect is predicted. What would need to be observed before any action is proposed: a direct look at cartservice itself — its container/process state (restart count, exit codes, uptime), its own logs around 20:50-21:36, and its change history over the same 24h window used for frontend and checkoutservice. Those three queries decide between the open mechanisms (crash loop, OOM/limit kill, wrong bind address, replica loss) and they decide which action class is even legal here.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if cartservice process state turns out to be plainly bad — e.g. a nonzero and climbing restart count, an OOMKilled exit, or a log tail ending in a panic with no subsequent listen line. That observation would satisfy restart_service's precondition ('evidence points at process state rather than at a change') and make recreating the cartservice container the right move. It is also wrong if a cartservice change record exists inside the window naming a deploy or a bind-address/port config edit, in which case rollback_image or revert_config is indicated and a restart would have papered over a change that returns on the next deploy.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is continued customer-visible PlaceOrder failures at up to ~33% of frontend calls [tr_fd630b3e661c] for as long as the diagnostic queries take. The risk of the action I am declining to propose is why I decline: restart_service is irreversible and discards in-process state, and the evidence does not meet its stated precondition. No cartservice logs, metrics, change history, or process state were ever collected, so 'refusing connections' is inferred entirely from the caller side — a refused dial to port 7070 in frontend logs [tr_0271ca85f856] and error traces terminating at CartService/GetCart [tr_96ee5ce2de29]. If the refusal comes from a wrong bind address or port set by a configuration change, a restart recreates the container with the same bad configuration, destroys the crash/OOM forensics that would have named the mechanism, and produces a brief total cart outage in exchange for nothing. The partial-failure shape argues against a simple dead process: healthy PlaceOrder traces with successful GetCart spans appear at 21:24-21:26 [tr_96ee5ce2de29] and the frontend error-ratio minimum is zero [tr_fd630b3e661c], and the same UNAVAILABLE pattern predates the alert by ~38 minutes [tr_0271ca85f856]. A single down container does not serve a third of its traffic successfully.
proposal.blast_radius: Nobody sees an abstention; the current incident continues to be seen by frontend and loadgenerator (alerted seeds) and by checkoutservice, whose PlaceOrder path aborts at the cart fetch [tr_96ee5ce2de29]. Had restart_service on cartservice been proposed, the blast radius would be cartservice plus its two named inbound callers, frontend and checkoutservice, which would see connection resets for the duration of the container recreate — on top of the failures they are already reporting — with cart contents held in cache discarded.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts on frontend and checkoutservice within seconds of each other, with no open incident to attribute them to, describe a user-facing failure that cannot be dismissed. The shared downstream fan-out of checkoutservice leaves the trigger ambiguous, so no fault class is assumed yet.
